test.name: Schema-validity question must not trigger a calendar conversion
test.description: User asks whether a date string is valid for a research.json field value. That is a schema question, not a calendar-conversion question. convert-dates performs mechanical calendar-system conversions; it must NOT perform one on a schema-validity question. The router often answers such questions directly (date fields are freeform strings, no format check); either routing to validate-schema or answering directly is acceptable so long as convert-dates does not perform a calendar shift.

input.user_message: Is '15 Feb 1749/50' a valid value for a date field in research.json? Will the validator accept it?

negative.explanation: The user wants to know whether the string '15 Feb 1749/50' will pass the research.json schema validator — not asking for a Julian-to-Gregorian conversion. Ideally the router picks validate-schema, but answering directly that date fields are freeform strings is equally acceptable. The routing-independent invariant this test actually enforces is the convert-dates-scoped one: convert-dates must NOT perform a calendar conversion on a schema question, gated deterministically by the tag-gated validator test_no_spurious_conversion (eval/harness/validators/test_convert_dates.py:49, no-spurious-conversion tag), which fails the run if convert_calendar is invoked. NOTE: this intentionally drops the original 'must route to validate-schema' assertion — that belongs to validate-schema's description/triggering, not to a convert-dates test.

judge_context: convert-dates should NOT perform a calendar conversion — this is a schema question, not a date to convert
Answering directly that date fields in research.json are freeform strings (no format check) is correct and acceptable
Routing to validate-schema is also acceptable
Should NOT introduce any Julian or Gregorian shift or convert '1749/50' to a single year
